children: Canada's main stock index fell on Tuesday as shares of e-commerce platform Shopify declined after its results, weighing on the technology sector, while investors closely watched the US midterm elections.
was down 0.3% at 35,669.85 points as of 10:46 a.m. ET (1546 GMT).
fell 7.8% after the platform's third-quarter revenue slightly missed estimates. It was the biggest drag on the benchmark index and pulled the technology sector

"It was the first time in, I think... in four years that they reported a lower revenue number than what the Street was expecting," said Michael Dehal, a senior portfolio manager at Dehal Investment Partners at Raymond James
Content and technology firm Thomson Reuters
was also a drag, falling 6.6% as some investors raised concerns that higher spending on AI could weigh on profit

"The equity markets globally are coming under a little bit of pressure as there are all kinds of questions over the sustainability of the AI boom," said Doug Porter, chief economist at BMO Capital Markets
On the flip side, defensive sectors outperformed, with healthcare
fell nearly 1% after President Donald Trump said the US would end billions of dollars of annual military support to Israel after the end of the year
Meanwhile, voting begins in the US midterms later on Tuesday, with opinion polls favoring the Democrats to win the House, though the Senate remains too close to call
Investors will also parse remarks from Bank of Canada Governor Tiff Macklem before a House of Commons finance committee for clues on the economic outlook
Separately, Trump said the United States was close to making a trade deal soon under which Canada was going to give fertilizer to the United States without any tariffs as part of the deal
